Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Central Commercial Registry for name certification and the Provincial Commercial Registry of the registered office (Registro Mercantil Central / Registro Mercantil Provincial), under the Directorate General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith of the Ministry of Justice; notarial authority intervenes in the deed.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital) — Book I Title V (Articles 22-58, single-member provisions included) and Book I Title VI (Articles 209-250 on the administrative body).

Formation / constitutional filings

Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) authorized by a Notary, followed by mandatory inscription in the Provincial Commercial Registry.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 40 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Standard SL capital is EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and paid up in cash at constitution; under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) the SL may be formed with EUR 1 initial capital, subject to a mandatory allocation of 20% of annual net profits to the legal reserve until EUR 3,000 is reached. Payment must be evidenced by a notary or by a bank certificate of deposit (cuenta de capital) opened in the company's name.

Funding & unlock path: Fire Safety Certificate (Certificado de Protección contra Incendios) issued under the Fire Protection Installations Regulation (RIPCI, Royal Decree 513/2017) with mandatory periodic inspections; structural load certificate and hydraulic pressure tests for process vessels; occupational risk prevention assessment under Law 31/1995 performed by an accredited external prevention service (Servicio de Prevención Ajeno), including health surveillance for operators exposed to heparin dust and chemical agents, and GMP-compliant cleanroom clearance verified by AEMPS.

Paid-in capital rule: Standard SL capital is EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and paid up in cash at constitution; under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) the SL may be formed with EUR 1 initial capital, subject to a mandatory allocation of 20% of annual net profits to the legal reserve until EUR 3,000 is reached. Payment must be evidenced by a notary or by a bank certificate of deposit (cuenta de capital) opened in the company's name.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); e-portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the tax identification procedure begins with the issuance of a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by AEAT before the deed of incorporation is executed before a notary. The provisional NIF is included in stockholder formalities, and after incorporation the entity has one month to apply for the definitive corporate NIF once registered in the Mercantile Registry. For non-resident founders or foreign shareholders, a tax representative resident in Spain may be required; the foreign entity must obtain a non-resident NIF before it can validly hold shares or carry out taxable acts in Spain. The definitive corporate NIF for an SL typically uses the letter B followed by eight digits. The same NIF is used as the Spanish VAT identification number (IVA NIF), and an IVA registration application (Modelo 036/037) must be filed to activate taxable activity before the first supply of goods or services. Foreign entities also appoint an AEAT-designated authorised representative where automatic exchanges or tax audits so require.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the tax identification procedure begins with the issuance of a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by AEAT before the deed of incorporation is executed before a notary. The provisional NIF is included in stockholder formalities, and after incorporation the entity has one month to apply for the definitive corporate NIF once registered in the Mercantile Registry. For non-resident founders or foreign shareholders, a tax representative resident in Spain may be required; the foreign entity must obtain a non-resident NIF before it can validly hold shares or carry out taxable acts in Spain. The definitive corporate NIF for an SL typically uses the letter B followed by eight digits. The same NIF is used as the Spanish VAT identification number (IVA NIF), and an IVA registration application (Modelo 036/037) must be filed to activate taxable activity before the first supply of goods or services. Foreign entities also appoint an AEAT-designated authorised representative where automatic exchanges or tax audits so require.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime. A Spanish SL is always a corporation subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) under Ley 27/2014. Available elections include: (i) the Spanish group taxation regime (consolidación fiscal) under Articles 61 et seq., which is irreversible for 10 years and requires a resident parent entity holding directly or indirectly at least 90% of the SL equity; (ii) the VAT group election (grupo de entidades) available to enterprises linked financially, economically or organisationally; (iii) the reduced 15% CIT rate for newly created SLs in the first tax period and the next one in which they obtain positive profits, provided they do not qualify as shell/patrimonial entities; (iv) optional accelerated depreciation and tax amortisation elections, including free depreciation for environmentally efficient assets; (v) the patent box and R&D tax credit regimes, which require formal recognition in the annual CIT return; and (vi) the Spanish transposition of ATAD anti-hybrid rules contains no elective mechanism — the deduction mismatch is disallowed mechanically where a hybrid instrument or entity triggers double deduction, deduction-without-inclusion, or imported mismatches.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR 0 — Spain applies no general VAT registration threshold. Any person habitually carrying out taxable economic activities within the Spanish VAT territory must file Modelo 036/037 and obtain an IVA NIF before commencing activity. For intra-EU distance sales of goods by a supplier established in another Member State, a special cross-border EUR 10,000 exemption threshold exists, once breached Spain becomes the place of supply and registration in Spain is mandatory. For the exporting Spanish SL, the zero-rated export regime applies directly without turnover threshold.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Act, exports of tangible goods to non-EU destinations are zero-rated when the goods physically leave the Spanish/EU VAT territory through customs formalities within 3 months from the tax point, and the export is performed by the exporting SL (or an authorised carrier acting on its behalf) evidenced by a valid Single Administrative Document (DUA) accepted by Customs. Accordingly, heparin sodium anticoagulant exported from Spain to Latin American or other non-EU customers is eligible for 0% IVA provided delivery is an export sale, the exporter keeps full shipping evidence, and the transaction is not treated as an intra-EU supply. Services directly related to exported goods, such as contract analysis, quality testing and ancillary transport services, may also qualify for zero-rating under Article 22 LIVA if they are rendered directly to the exporter and the goods have been definitively exported. The exporter may simultaneously claim the deduction/refund of input VAT incurred on raw materials, extraction equipment and factory overheads by including the export turnover in Modelo 303/390 while attaching the required supporting documentation.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA / Single Administrative Document)
  • Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (airway bill / CMR road consignment note)
  • Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the Spanish bank account in the exporter's name
  • Commercial invoice and detailed packing list
  • AEMPS export licence for the medicinal substance (heparin sodium starting material)
  • Evidence of physical departure from Spanish/EU territory (port terminal receipt, customs seal, scan manifests)
  • Preferential origin certificate (EUR.1, ATR or invoice declaration) only when claiming origin-based customs benefits — not required solely for VAT zero-rating

Spain mandates electronic invoicing between entrepreneurs and professionals under Ley Crea y Crece (Royal Decree 1007/2023), using interoperable formats such as Facturae deriving from the European standard. The SII (Sistema de Suministro Inmediato de Información) obliges large taxpayers with VAT turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000, and certain VAT groups and tributary-transparent entities, to submit electronic billing records to AEAT within 4 calendar days from issue/receipt (extension to 8 calendar days monthly). The Verifactu regulation requires compliant software to preserve invoice integrity and auditability. For public sector invoices, Facturae with a QR digital stamp is mandatory. Spain operates a non-intrusive fiscal clearance model rather than pre-clearance; AEAT accepts e-invoices after issuance but maintains real-time access for high-risk exporters.

Export zero-rating refunds are intensely scrutinised through verification of B/L dates, customs exit stamps and bank remittance proofs. If AEAT establishes that goods did not physically leave Spain or the documentation is forged, the exporter loses the zero rate, input VAT previously refunded is clawed back with late payment interest, and the tax liability is recalculated at 21%. Under Article 191 of Ley General Tributaria (LGT), the penalty ranges from 50% to 100% of the evaded VAT depending on whether there was intentional misconduct. If a false invoice or fictitious export is used to obtain a refund exceeding EUR 120,000 in any one tax period, the conduct may constitute criminal tax fraud under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code carrying imprisonment of one to six years and monetary fines of up to six times the defrauded amount. In addition, the exporter's status as a reliable taxable person may be withdrawn, with forced electronic invoicing and disallowance of future refunds until guarantees are posted.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

The euro is fully convertible. Spain applies the EU Treaty framework for free movement of capital and imposes no exchange-control restrictions on current payments, capital transfers, profit remittances, dividend distributions, or purchasing of foreign currency. Non-EEA foreign direct investment in an SL is subject to post-closing statistical registration with the Foreign Investment Registry; ordinary profit remittance requires only standard banking channels and proof of applicable corporate tax withholdings, not central-bank authorisation.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no statutory surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters may invoice in EUR or any freely convertible currency, retain proceeds in foreign-currency accounts with Spanish banks, and settle directly through commercial banks. Cross-border payments above the statutory statistical threshold (EUR 50,000) must be reported under the Spanish declaration of foreign operations (Declaración de Operaciones con el Exterior) for balance-of-payments statistics, but no conversion or surrender obligation applies.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) within the Eurosystem, under the European Central Bank's monetary policy authority; cross-border transaction and balance-of-payments reporting is administered jointly with the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. An offshore digital EMI that does not hold an EU/EEA electronic-money institution license cannot legally maintain payment accounts for a Spanish SL under the Spanish Payments Law and PSD2. Even an EEA-authorized EMI can serve only as a supplementary account for low-value open-account payments; it cannot provide the documentary credit, guarantee, or multi-currency trade-clearing infrastructure required for active pharmaceutical ingredient distribution. The primary treasury account must be held with a tier-1 Spanish commercial bank.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident UBO structure with multi-layer shareholdings and inconsistent source of wealth

Root cause: Non-resident UBO structure with multi-layer shareholdings and inconsistent source of wealth

Defense evidence: Company registry certificates, notarised passports, UBO declaration form, corporate organisation chart, bank statements of the sending shareholder, source-of-wealth statement, tax residence certificates, and a legal opinion from an EU-qualified attorney.
High-value cross-border wire activity to Latin America involving pharmaco-chemical substances

Root cause: High-value cross-border wire activity to Latin America involving pharmaco-chemical substances

Defense evidence: Signed commercial contracts, invoices, Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices (AEMPS) licences, EU-GMP certificates, customs declarations, bills of lading, packing lists, quality certificates, import/export permits, and a written narrative explaining the commercial flow.
Substance mismatch: virtual office, limited payroll, or transaction volumes disproportionate to operational footprint

Root cause: Substance mismatch: virtual office, limited payroll, or transaction volumes disproportionate to operational footprint

Defense evidence: Lease agreement or full-service office contract, payroll registers, audited financial statements, VAT returns, corporate tax filings, inventory and warehouse records, production facility inspection reports, and an operational substance questionnaire signed by the director.
Sanctions-list proximity, PEP appearance, or indirect payment routing through offshore financial centres

Root cause: Sanctions-list proximity, PEP appearance, or indirect payment routing through offshore financial centres

Defense evidence: Enhanced due diligence questionnaire, professional sanctions and PEP screening results, sworn statement on beneficial ownership, complete transaction rationale, external auditor confirmation, and confirmation from the legal department that no sanctioned entity or individual is involved in any link of the payment chain.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant inbound capital injections must be executed as a SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR to the SL's Spanish IBAN, or as a SWIFT MT103 wire for non-euro currencies. The remittance must include a clear purpose code — 'Capital Injection / Subscription of Capital' — and the SL's tax identification number (NIF). Where a non-EEA investor injects equity or shareholder loans, the corresponding foreign investment declaration must be filed with the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business and, when the amount exceeds EUR 50,000, the balance-of-payments statistical declaration must be submitted to Banco de España. Verification is completed by matching the incoming funds to the executed capital increase deed, notarised shareholders' resolution, and the registry filing before the funds can be released for operating expenditures.Outbound treasury clearing for heparin raw-material and finished-anticoagulant trade should use: (1) documentary irrevocable Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600, ideally confirmed, for large-ticket cross-border sale/purchase contracts; (2) SWIFT MT103 for open-account settlements to non-EU suppliers and customers; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-denominated payments to EU counterparties; and (4) documentary collection (D/P or D/A) where an LC is not commercially required. All disbursements must be paired with invoices, transport documents, customs export declarations, AEMPS health licences, and any applicable sanitary certificates to avoid delayed processing.Outright FX forwards with a Spanish or EU-authorised credit institution in EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/MXN and other trade-relevant pairsFX swaps and roll-over contractsPlain vanilla FX options and zero-cost collarsCross-currency interest rate swaps under ISDA master agreements for medium-term commercial debtNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only on emerging-market currencies with restricted physical delivery in the EU (e.g., offshore CNY, certain LatAm currencies), executed strictly as commercial hedging instruments

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. An offshore digital EMI that does not hold an EU/EEA electronic-money institution license cannot legally maintain payment accounts for a Spanish SL under the Spanish Payments Law and PSD2. Even an EEA-authorized EMI can serve only as a supplementary account for low-value open-account payments; it cannot provide the documentary credit, guarantee, or multi-currency trade-clearing infrastructure required for active pharmaceutical ingredient distribution. The primary treasury account must be held with a tier-1 Spanish commercial bank.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% standard; 15% for newly created eligible small entities during first two taxable years; 30% for credit institutions and oil/gas entities where applicable

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% domestic statutory rate on dividends paid from the Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when the recipient is a qualifying EU/EEA company; further reduced by DTAs, often 0–15% depending on treaty and holding percentage.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year end; for calendar-year taxpayers, due 1–25 July.

Deadline: · Frequency:

First 20 calendar days of April, October and December (for the 1st, 3rd and 10-month periods respectively).

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 001 Cuenta de Pérdidas y Ganancias: accounting profit or loss before corporate income tax per Spanish GAAP. Reserved to the resident SL; non-resident beneficial owners do not file this field; their withholding obligations are addressed separately via recipient returns. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 002 Correcciones al resultado contable: permanent and temporary base adjustments (e.g., non-deductible provisions, fair value changes, transfer pricing adjustments). N/A for non-residents; SL management must document arm's length corrections for any cross-border transactions. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 003 Base imponible ajustada: taxable income after accounting adjustments and before loss compensation. N/A; resident company only. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 004 Compensación de bases imponibles negativas: carryforward offset of historical tax losses. N/A; loss carryforward is unrestricted under Spanish law for entities with ordinary substance. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 005 Base imponible: resulting taxable base after applying Box 004. N/A. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 006 Tipo de gravamen aplicable: the tax rate applied (standard 25%, reduced 15%, special 30%, or treaty configuration). N/A for non-resident payees; resident SL determines its own rate. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 007 Cuota íntegra: gross tax liability before deductions and credits. N/A. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 008 Deducciones y bonificaciones: domestic and treaty-related tax credits, R&D credits, and double-tax relief. N/A; treaty relief for non-residents is claimed by them, not the SL. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 009 Cuota líquida: tax liability after applying deductions and credits. N/A. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 010 Retenciones, pagos fraccionados y pagos a cuenta: withheld tax, advance payments, and corporate prepayments made during the year. For dividends, interest or royalties paid to non-residents, the SL must include withholdings separately and report to AEAT; non-resident taxpayers use Form 210. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 011 Resultado de la declaración: the net amount either to be paid or refunded. N/A; final settlement is the SL's sole obligation. Late filing triggers surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6), 15% (within 12), 20% (after 12) plus late-payment interest; fixed minimum penalty of €200 where no tax is due; unjustified penalties under LGT Art. 191 add 50–200% on the unpaid quota.
Box 1 Base declarada: taxable base of the fraction of the year (per previous-year tax return or actual profit of the period). N/A; only the resident SL files Modelo 202. Late filing/underpayment of advance instalments incurs surcharge of 5% plus late-payment interest; recurrent omissions can lead to consolidated penalty proceedings and seizure of bank balances.
Box 2 Porcentaje de cálculo: 18% for ordinary entities; 25% for entities with net turnover ≥ €10 million in the previous year. N/A. Late filing/underpayment of advance instalments incurs surcharge of 5% plus late-payment interest; recurrent omissions can lead to consolidated penalty proceedings and seizure of bank balances.
Box 3 Resultado del pago fraccionado: computed advance amount. N/A. Late filing/underpayment of advance instalments incurs surcharge of 5% plus late-payment interest; recurrent omissions can lead to consolidated penalty proceedings and seizure of bank balances.
Box 4 Retenciones y pagos a cuenta deducibles: credits against the advance amount. N/A. Late filing/underpayment of advance instalments incurs surcharge of 5% plus late-payment interest; recurrent omissions can lead to consolidated penalty proceedings and seizure of bank balances.
Box 5 Importe a ingresar: net amount payable to the Spanish treasury. N/A. Late filing/underpayment of advance instalments incurs surcharge of 5% plus late-payment interest; recurrent omissions can lead to consolidated penalty proceedings and seizure of bank balances.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: €10,000,000 net turnover in the preceding year triggers mandatory maintenance of Spanish Local File; entities belonging to a multinational group with consolidated revenue of at least €750,000,000 must additionally prepare and file the Master File.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to Caribbean financial centres; however, Spanish GAAR (LIS Art. 15) and jurisprudence enforce substance-over-form, denying tax benefits to entities lacking genuine establishment, employees, premises, and entrepreneurial activity. For treaty/MLI applications, the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) and applicable LOB clauses require that the Spanish SL extracting heparin has real operational substance in Spain; phantom royalty or procurement structures will be recharacterised and stripped of treaty protection.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion / Underdeclaration of Income

Statutory sanction: Tax debt plus surcharge of 50%–200% of the unpaid amount (LGT Art. 191); criminal tax fraud under Penal Code Art. 305 applies where the attributable defraudation exceeds €120,000 in one fiscal year, with penalties including imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and criminal fine of up to six times the defrauded amount; loss of tax credits and grants.

Director personal liability: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes under LGT Art. 43 when they knowingly participated in the concealment; criminal conviction triggers piercing of corporate veil, travel bans, arrest warrants, and attachment of personal assets for civil restitution.
Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance

Statutory sanction: AEAT disallows deductions, recharacterises transactions, and applies the GAAR penalty (LGT Art. 206) of 50%–100% of the improper tax benefit; administrative dissolution of the entity may be requested by the authorities; treaty benefits are denied for lack of economic substance under MLI/PPT.

Director personal liability: Directors can be subject to director disqualification orders, travel bans under criminal process, and personal civil recovery for funds dissipated through the shell; if the shell conceals assets from creditors, charges of insolvency fraud or money laundering may be brought.
Transfer Pricing Manipulation

Statutory sanction: Primary TP adjustment with increase in taxable base; penalty of 15% of the corrected amount (LIS Art. 18.13); late-payment interest; administrative fines for incomplete or omitted TP documentation of up to 2% of the transaction amount (minimum €1,500); where the adjustment exceeds €120,000, criminal tax fraud may be asserted.

Director personal liability: Directors who sign false Statements in TP documentation or Form 200 face personal liability for the corporate unpaid tax amounts; criminal penalties may include imprisonment for up to 5 years, travel restrictions, and seizure of director-owned assets.
Anti-Money Laundering (AML) / Non-Traceable Proceeds

Statutory sanction: AML Law 10/2010 penalties ranging up to €5,000,000 or 2% of comparable turnover for serious/very serious infractions; criminal money laundering under Penal Code Art. 301 carries imprisonment of 1 to 6 years and confiscation of proceeds; bank freezing and debarment from government procurement are additional risks.

Director personal liability: Directors may be criminally prosecuted as culpable officers; preventive detention or travel bans are common where flight risk exists; personal assets are subject to asset forfeiture under Spanish Anti-Money Laundering seizure rules, and corporate veil can be pierced for complicity.
